judgment_text:
Prayer : Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of writ of certiorarified Mandamus, calling for the records pertaining to the impugned order in No. 1029/Tha.ku.2/2026, dated 21-4-2026 on the file of the second respondent and quash the same as bad in law and consequently direct the first and second respondents to grant emergency leave without escort to the petitioner's husband, namely, Dineshkumar S/o Thangapandi (C.P. No. 1276, PID No. 284858), now confined in Madurai Central Prison, based on the petitioner's representation dated 26-3-2026.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

N. Anand Venkatesh, J.:— This writ petition has been filed challenging the impugned proceedings of the second respondent made in No. 1029/Tha.ku.2/2026, dated 21-4-2026, wherein the second respondent while granting emergency leave to the convict imposed a condition that he will be accompanied by an escort. This condition has been put to challenge in the present writ petition.

2. Heard the learned counsel on either side.

3. The petitioner is the wife of the convict. The convict is undergoing rigorous imprisonment at Madurai Central Prison for the offence under the NDPS Act. A representation was made by the petitioner to the effect that the convict's mother has been diagnosed with cancer and therefore, her health condition is deteriorating and therefore, sought for 15 days emergency leave for the convict.

4. The second respondent through the impugned proceedings dated 21-4-2026 granted six days emergency leave with escort. The same has been put to challenge in the present writ petition.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that 15 days emergency leave is required for the convict, since his mother has been diagnosed with cancer and her health condition is very serious. To substantiate the same, the learned counsel relied upon the medical grounds that forms part of the paper book.

6. We have carefully gone through the medical records. In our considered view, for the present, we are only inclined to modify the condition that has been imposed by the second respondent insofar as the convict being accompanied by an escort during the entire period of emergency leave. Considering the reasons for which the emergency leave has been sought for, we deem it fit to interfere only with that condition.

7. In view of the above, the condition imposed by the second respondent is modified to the effect that the convict will report before the fourth respondent daily at 06.00 p.m., during the entire period of emergency leave. Apart from that condition, the convict is permitted to submit the sureties before the Superintendent of Prison, Central Prison, Madurai, instead of executing the sureties before the Tahsildar and two sureties shall be the family members of the convict. The other conditions imposed by the second respondent shall stand as it is.

8. This Writ Petition (Criminal) is disposed in the above terms.
